acceptance_signals: One internal policy definition covers all eight unique MCP tools and removes duplicated identity, discovery-gate, and routing classification.
Clients without form elicitation still discover exactly six base tools and form-capable clients still discover exactly eight tools in the existing order.
Deterministic tests prove catalog, discovery gate, ordinary dispatch, interactive form routing, effect classification, enforcement ownership, and downstream non-grants remain in parity.
Lifecycle, task, scope, evidence, and human-decision checks remain fresh call-time or effect-boundary enforcement and are not duplicated as metadata predicates.
Current MCP public behavior remains unchanged and relevant focused and full repository validation pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-1eb71c1b97204842b144caf08c9016da and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Consolidate the existing AgentGov MCP tool identity, discovery gate, routing class, effect metadata, enforcement ownership, and downstream non-grants into one minimal internal policy surface, then add deterministic parity tests while preserving all current runtime behavior and call-time governance checks.

items: A metadata registry could become a second source of truth unless names, discovery gates, and route classification are derived from it.
Refactoring form routing could accidentally change the interactive native elicitation path.
Over-modeling lifecycle predicates would enlarge the Adapter and duplicate existing enforcement.
Reviewed assumption: The current six-base and eight-form-capable tool catalogs are the intended development-source behavior.
Reviewed assumption: This change requires no Kernel ontology, public release identity, Git execution, authority registry, or audit-event expansion.
Reviewed assumption: Historical version evidence remains historical; only current MCP contract guidance and current repository reality need clarification.

title: Add deterministic MCP tool contract parity
